one_line: chunk-boundary parse failure across language tag
reason: The StreamParser throws when a language tag like @nl-nl is split across two HTTP response chunks. The defect is in consuming the input, not in writing it; §3.1 admits only written-output defects, so the record is out of scope by the paper's own criterion. Carried as a side finding next to jsonld.js #584, not as a record.

`turtle` warns about illegal characters while parsing a legal UTF-8 IRI. The defect is in reading, not writing, which puts it out of scope under §3.1; the class label it carried (C5, format mislabelling) also does not fit the issue text. Withdrawn for both reasons.

one_line: lone surrogate accepted in a \u escape sequence
reason: The report asks the tokenizer to reject illegal surrogate escape sequences. Jena's own text on the follow-up records that it 'has not written such \u and \U escape sequences', so nothing defective is written; the defect is in accepting the input. Out of scope under §3.1 as a read-side item. Withdrawn in the 2026-10-11 revision.

A specification follow-up for the parsers: reject lone surrogates, or low-high pairs, written as \u / \U escapes. It constrains what the parser accepts, not what the writer emits, and is out of scope under §3.1 for the same reason as N3.js 578. Withdrawn in the 2026-10-11 revision.
